page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a high-capacity, storage-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 768.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is a major feature of this instance, which comes bundled with 23,038 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the L96as_v4 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU evaluations. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read-only cached bandwidth of 7,287.47 GB/sec, alongside strong uncached read and write speeds. Cryptographic capabilities are highly efficient, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions, resulting in top-tier performance in Passmark encryption tests. Multi-threaded decompression and software compilation also rank in the top 10%, while database operations and Redis SET throughput place in the top 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L96as_v4 offers high resource density by combining massive local NVMe storage with a high-core AMD EPYC processor, reducing the need for external storage attachments for I/O-heavy workloads. The lack of a dedicated GPU makes it less suitable for heavy model training, though it maintains strong prompt processing speeds for small and medium LLM inference. This instance is highly suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, data warehousing, high-throughput web serving, and intensive multi-threaded engineering simulations.
